![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_14_fig_1.png)

In figure 3, $ABC$ is a triangle in which $BD$ is a perpendicular to $AC$. Given that $AC = 30$ cm, $AB = 10$ cm and $AD = 6$ cm.

Find:

figures.legende: Figure 3: triangle ABC with D on AC, BD perpendicular to AC; AB = 10 cm, AD = 6 cm, AC = 30 cm.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Triangle $ABD$ has a right angle at $D$, so by Pythagoras' theorem:

$BD^2 = AB^2 - AD^2 = 10^2 - 6^2 = 100 - 36 = 64$

$BD = \sqrt{64} = 8$ cm.

**$BD = 8$ cm.**

$D$ lies on $AC$, so $DC = AC - AD = 30 - 6 = 24$ cm.

**$DC = 24$ cm.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The angle $DCB$. *[7 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the right-angled triangle $BDC$: $\tan\angle DCB = \dfrac{BD}{DC}=\dfrac{8}{24}=\dfrac{1}{3}$.

$\angle DCB = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac13\right)=18.43^\circ$.

**$\angle DCB \approx 18.4^\circ$.**
